description: This topic explains the meaning and importance of movement and locomotion, the structure and functions of the human skeleton, types of joints and muscles, and how animals such as fish and birds move.

mcq.questionText: What is the difference between movement and locomotion?

options.text: Movement is the change of position of a whole organism, while locomotion is part movement
Movement is the change of position of part of an organism, while locomotion is movement of the whole organism from one place to another
Movement and locomotion mean exactly the same thing
Locomotion only happens in plants and movement only in animals

mcq.explanation: Movement is a change in position of a part of the body, while locomotion is the movement of the whole organism from one place to another.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a function of the human skeleton?
mcq.explanation: The skeleton supports the body, protects organs, allows movement, gives shape and makes blood cells, but it does not produce digestive enzymes.

mcq.questionText: Which part of the skeleton belongs to the axial skeleton?
mcq.explanation: The axial skeleton includes the skull, vertebral column, ribs and sternum. Limbs and girdles belong to the appendicular skeleton.

mcq.questionText: The appendicular skeleton is made up of which of the following?
mcq.explanation: The appendicular skeleton consists of the bones of the limbs (arms and legs) together with the pectoral and pelvic girdles.

mcq.questionText: Which type of joint is found at the elbow?
mcq.explanation: The elbow is a hinge joint that allows movement in one plane, like the opening and closing of a door.

mcq.questionText: Which joint allows movement in all directions?
mcq.explanation: A ball-and-socket joint, such as the hip and shoulder, allows movement in all directions (rotation).

mcq.questionText: Which structure connects a muscle to a bone?
mcq.explanation: Tendons connect muscles to bones, while ligaments connect bone to bone at a joint.

mcq.questionText: What is the main role of synovial fluid in a movable joint?

options.text: To lubricate the joint and reduce friction

mcq.explanation: Synovial fluid lubricates the joint, reduces friction between bones and absorbs shock during movement.

mcq.questionText: When the biceps muscle contracts, what happens to the arm?

options.text: The arm bends at the elbow
The arm becomes fixed and cannot move

mcq.explanation: When the biceps contracts it pulls the lower arm upwards, bending (flexing) the arm at the elbow.

mcq.questionText: Biceps and triceps are described as antagonistic muscles because they:

options.text: Work in opposite directions to move the same bone
Are both attached only to soft tissue

mcq.explanation: Antagonistic muscles work in opposite directions; when one contracts the other relaxes, allowing the bone to move back and forth.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an example of an immovable (fixed) joint?

options.text: Joint between the bones of the skull

mcq.explanation: The joints (sutures) between the bones of the skull are fixed (immovable) and allow no movement.

mcq.questionText: Which type of joint is found between the vertebrae of the backbone?
mcq.explanation: The joints between vertebrae are slightly movable, allowing limited bending and twisting of the backbone.

mcq.questionText: What is the main function of cartilage at the ends of bones in a joint?

options.text: To reduce friction and act as a cushion between bones

mcq.explanation: Cartilage covers the ends of bones at a joint, reducing friction and acting as a cushion that absorbs shock.

mcq.questionText: Which body structure helps fish to move and balance in water?
mcq.explanation: Fish use their fins for balance and steering and their muscular tail to push against the water for forward movement.

mcq.questionText: Which feature of birds is mainly an adaptation for flight?

options.text: Light hollow bones and strong wing muscles

mcq.explanation: Birds have light hollow bones, feathers and powerful breast (wing) muscles, which are adaptations that make flight possible.

fib.questionText: The movement of the whole organism from one place to another is called _____.
fib.explanation: Locomotion is the movement of an entire organism from one place to another, for example walking or swimming.

fib.questionText: The skull, vertebral column, ribs and sternum form the _____ skeleton.
fib.explanation: The axial skeleton forms the central axis of the body and includes the skull, vertebral column, ribs and sternum.

fib.questionText: Bones are connected to other bones at a joint by tough fibres called _____.
fib.explanation: Ligaments are strong fibres that hold bones together at a joint.

fib.questionText: Muscles are attached to bones by structures called _____.
fib.explanation: Tendons join muscles to bones so that muscle contraction can move the bones.

fib.questionText: The fluid that lubricates a movable joint and reduces friction is called _____ fluid.
fib.explanation: Synovial fluid fills movable joints, lubricating them and reducing friction during movement.

fib.questionText: The type of joint found at the hip and shoulder that allows movement in all directions is the _____ joint.
fib.explanation: The ball-and-socket joint allows rotation and movement in all directions, found at the hip and shoulder.

fib.questionText: The muscle that contracts to straighten the arm at the elbow is the _____.
fib.explanation: The triceps contracts to straighten (extend) the arm while the biceps relaxes.

fib.questionText: A pair of muscles that work in opposite directions, such as the biceps and triceps, are called _____ muscles.
fib.explanation: Antagonistic muscles work against each other; when one contracts the other relaxes.

fib.questionText: Soft connective tissue that covers the ends of bones and acts as a cushion is called _____.
fib.explanation: Cartilage covers bone ends at joints, reducing friction and absorbing shock.

fib.questionText: Fish use their muscular _____ to push against water for forward movement.
fib.explanation: The tail of a fish pushes against the water to propel the fish forward, while fins help with balance and steering.

tf.questionText: Locomotion means the movement of the whole organism from one place to another.
tf.explanation: Locomotion is correctly defined as the movement of an entire organism from one place to another.

tf.questionText: The skeleton protects delicate organs such as the brain and the heart.
tf.explanation: The skull protects the brain and the rib cage protects the heart and lungs.

tf.questionText: The femur and humerus are part of the axial skeleton.
tf.explanation: The femur and humerus are limb bones, so they belong to the appendicular skeleton, not the axial skeleton.
Ligaments connect bone to bone; tendons connect muscle to bone.

tf.questionText: The joints between the bones of the skull are immovable.
tf.explanation: The skull bones are joined by fixed (immovable) joints called sutures.

tf.questionText: A hinge joint allows movement in all directions.
tf.explanation: A hinge joint, such as the elbow or knee, allows movement in only one plane; the ball-and-socket joint allows movement in all directions.

tf.questionText: Synovial fluid increases friction inside a joint.
tf.explanation: Synovial fluid reduces friction and lubricates the joint, making movement smooth.

tf.questionText: When the biceps contracts, the triceps relaxes.
tf.explanation: Biceps and triceps are antagonistic; while one contracts the other relaxes.

tf.questionText: Some bones produce blood cells inside their bone marrow.
tf.explanation: Red bone marrow inside certain bones produces red and white blood cells.

tf.questionText: Birds have heavy solid bones to help them fly.
tf.explanation: Birds have light hollow bones which reduce body weight and make flight easier.

summary.questionText: State the difference between movement and locomotion.
summary.correctAnswer: Movement is a change of position of a part of the body, while locomotion is the movement of the whole organism from one place to another.
summary.explanation: This distinguishes part movement from whole-body movement, a key definition in this topic.

summary.questionText: List the main functions of the human skeleton.
summary.correctAnswer: Support, protection of organs, movement, giving body shape, and production of blood cells.
summary.explanation: These are the five main functions of the skeleton in the human body.

summary.questionText: Name the parts that make up the axial skeleton.
summary.correctAnswer: The skull, vertebral column, ribs and sternum.
summary.explanation: The axial skeleton forms the central supporting axis of the body.

summary.questionText: Name the parts that make up the appendicular skeleton.
summary.correctAnswer: The limbs (arms and legs) and the girdles (pectoral and pelvic girdles).
summary.explanation: The appendicular skeleton is mainly involved in locomotion and limb movement.

summary.questionText: Give one example each of a ball-and-socket joint and a hinge joint.
summary.correctAnswer: Ball-and-socket: hip or shoulder; hinge: elbow or knee.
summary.explanation: Ball-and-socket joints rotate freely, while hinge joints move in one plane.

summary.questionText: Explain the difference between a tendon and a ligament.
summary.correctAnswer: A tendon connects muscle to bone, while a ligament connects bone to bone.
summary.explanation: Both are connective tissues but they join different structures at and around a joint.

summary.questionText: State two roles of synovial fluid in a movable joint.
summary.correctAnswer: It lubricates the joint to reduce friction and it absorbs shock during movement.
summary.explanation: Synovial fluid keeps movable joints working smoothly and protects the bone ends.

summary.questionText: Explain how antagonistic muscles move the arm at the elbow.
summary.correctAnswer: When the biceps contracts and the triceps relaxes the arm bends; when the triceps contracts and the biceps relaxes the arm straightens.
summary.explanation: Antagonistic pairs pull bones in opposite directions because muscles can only pull, not push.

summary.questionText: Describe the three main types of joints found in the human body.
summary.correctAnswer: Fixed (immovable) joints such as the skull sutures, slightly movable joints such as those between vertebrae, and freely movable (synovial) joints such as the elbow and hip.
summary.explanation: Joints are classified by how much movement they allow.

summary.questionText: Describe how a fish and a bird are adapted for locomotion.
summary.correctAnswer: A fish uses fins for balance and a muscular tail to push against water for swimming; a bird has light hollow bones, feathers and strong wing muscles for flight.
summary.explanation: Different animals have body structures suited to moving in their environment.

hoq.questionText: A footballer twists and lands badly, and the tough fibres that hold the bones together at the knee are torn. Which structure has most likely been injured?
hoq.explanation: Ligaments hold bone to bone at a joint, so a torn fibre connecting the knee bones is a ligament injury.

hoq.questionText: A patient cannot straighten the lower arm after an accident, although the biceps still works. Which muscle is most likely affected, and why?

options.text: The triceps, because it contracts to straighten the arm
The biceps, because it straightens the arm
The triceps, because it bends the arm
The biceps, because it relaxes the arm

hoq.explanation: The triceps contracts to straighten (extend) the arm, so if the arm cannot be straightened the triceps is most likely affected.

hoq.questionText: An elderly person feels pain and a grinding sensation in the hip because the smooth tissue covering the bone ends has worn away. Which structure has been damaged and what was its function?

options.text: Cartilage, which reduced friction and cushioned the bones
Bone marrow, which connected the bones

hoq.explanation: Cartilage covers the bone ends to reduce friction and cushion the joint; when it wears away the bones rub together causing pain.
